questions.question:
Which of the following are included in 'revenue receipts'?

(a) Tax Revenue

(b) Non-tax Revenue
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (a) and (b).**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Revenue receipts **are defined as those receipts that** neither increase a government's liabilities nor decrease its assets.**
 
• They are** routine and ongoing **in nature, and the government receives them as part of daily operations.
 
• **Taxes and other levies **collected by the Centre, **interest and dividends** received on investments, and fees and charges paid to the government for services are all considered **revenue receipts.**
 
• The **government's assets** **do not decrease **as a result of revenue collections.
 
• As a result, the government is unable to report the proceeds from the sale of a stake in a **public-sector business** as revenue because the sale of the holding reduced its assets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tax revenues and non-tax revenues** are the** two main sources** of income for the government.
 
• **Tax revenue:**
 
 
• It is the **total amount received** from all taxes and other** government-imposed levies.**
 
• Taxes are mandatory payments that **individuals and businesses** must make to the government without **expecting a direct benefit** in return.
 
 
 
• **Non Tax Revenues:**
 
 
• **Government receipts** from** all sources** other than tax receipts are referred to as non-tax revenue.
 
• **Interest, profits and dividends, fees, license fees, fines and penalties, gifts and grants, forfeitures, and special assessments **are the primary non-tax revenue streams.

questions.question: Honey is composed of water and two types of sugars: ______ and glucose.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**fructose.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Honey **is composed primarily of** water **and two sugars: **fructose and glucose**.
 
• **Enzymes, amino acids, B vitamins, vitamin C, minerals, and antioxidants** are also present in trace levels.
 
• A large portion of the antioxidants in honey are **flavonoids**.
 
• **The anti-inflammatory characteristic**s of flavonoids suggest they may offer some **health advantages.**
 
• **Fructose:**
 
 
• Fructose is a type of sugar known as a **monosaccharide.**
 
• Along with **glucose and some traces of galactose**, it is one of the three dietary monosaccharides that are** directly absorbed** into the blood following **digestion.**
 
• Because it is largely found naturally in many** fruits,** fructose is also referred to as** "fruit sugar."**
 
• It also naturally occurs in other plant-based foods like **vegetables, honey, sugar beets, and sugar cane.****​**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sucrose:**

 
 
• **Disaccharide sugar sucrose** is made up of the **subunits of glucose and fructose.**

 
 
• It is the** primary ingredient of white suga**r and is naturally generated by** plants.**
 
 
 
• Its chemical formula is **C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁.**
 
 
 
• **Dextrose:**
 
 
• A form of sugar called dextrose typically comes from** corn or wheat**.
 
• Dextrose is almost** identical to glucose**, which is the sugar found in the bloodstream.
 
 
 
• **Laevulose:**
 
 
• Laevulose is a** water-soluble white crystalline sugar **found in honey and a variety of fruits.

questions.question: Pattadakal, a UNESCO world heritage site, is located on the banks of River ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Malaprabha.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pattadakal,** a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is situated on the banks of the** Malaprabha River.**
 
• **It** provides evidence of the** wealth of Chalukyan architecture** from the **7th and 8th centuries.**
 
• It is renowned for its** intricately chiselled temples.**
 
• It comprises a collection of **10 significant temples,** each with a unique architectural style.
 
• The settlement was referred to as** "Perti gal"** by the **renowned geographer Ptolemy **(about 150 AD).
 
• It was even used as the **ceremonial centre** where** kings were crowned and commemorated**.
 
• The temple complex at Pattadakal features **Dravidian, Aryan, and a combination of the two architectural styles.**
 
• It is also the venue for the** Pattadakal Dance Festival **or **Chalukya Utsava **with performers from all over the world congregating here. ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tungabhadra:**

 
 
• The majority of the Tungabhadra River's course is in the Indian state of **Karnataka**.
 
• It then passes through the border states of** Telangana and Andhra Pradesh** until coming together with the **Krishna River **next to Gundimalla village in the Jogulamba Gadwal district of Telangana.
 
• The river's water is renowned for being sweet and is regarded as the **sweetest water in the entire world.**
 
 
 
• **Ghataprabha:**
 
 
• The Ghataprabha River, a significant** right-bank tributary of the Krishna River**, travels** 283 kilometres** east of Chikksangam before joining the Krishna River.
 
 
 
• **Bhima:**
 
 
• The Bhima River often referred to as the** Chandrabhaga River,** is a significant river in both** South and Western India.**
 
• It travels through the states of** Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Telangana **for **861 kilometers** before emptying into the Krishna River.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Women’s Indian Association established in Madras (Chennai)?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• At **Adayar, Madras, in 1917**, **Annie Besant, Margaret Cousins, Jeena Raja Dasa,** and others formed the **Women's Indian Association (WIA)**.
 
• The** aim** was to free women from the** dreadful conditions** they endured in **political and socio-economic affairs **in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
 
• The Association later evolved into a powerful force in the struggle against social problems like** child marriage, illiteracy, and the Devadasi system.**
 
• **Dorothy Jinarajadasa** got more involved in** theosophist internal politics **following **Besant's passing in 1933.**
 
• **Freedom fighter Muthulakshmi Reddy** served as **editor** of the WIA's monthly English journa**l "Stri-Dharma" from 1931 to 1940.** 
 
• WIA was the first women's association in India to present a** memorandum to the Round Table Conference **on** Women's Franchise **and her **Constitutional rights** as well as the initiator of the **first All Asian Women's Conference.**

questions.question: In which of the following years did the first Amendment Act of the Constitution of India come into force?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1951.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **1951 Constitution (First Amendment) Act **amended the **Fundamental Rights clauses **of the Indian Constitution in a number of ways. 
 
• It offered ways to** impose restrictions** on the **right to free speech and expression** and **supported laws **that** outlawed zamindari.**
 
• It was made clear that the** right to equalit**y does not exclude the passing of laws that give **"particular regard"** to society's **most vulnerable groups.**
 
• This Amendment established a precedent for **rewriting the Constitution** to** override judicial decisions** that** prevented the government** from
 
• carrying out its alleged obligations to **specific policies and programs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• A** constitution** is a collection of **guiding ideas or accepted precedents **that serve as the** foundation** for a polity, organization, etc.
 
• The** Indian Constitution **is credited to** Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar** as its **father.**
 
• On** 26 November 1949, **it was approved by the** Indian Constituent Assembly**, and on **26 January 1950**, it came into force.
 
• The** Government of India Act of 1935** was superseded by the constitution as the** primary law of the land,** transforming the **Dominion of India** into the **Republic of India.**

questions.question: If a table tennis game does not go up to deuce, then what is the maximum point to be earned by the winner?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**11.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Table tennis matches are currently played with a maximum of** 11 points**.
 
• The** winner** is the player or pair who first **scores 11 point**s unless both players or pairs **score 10 points (called deuce)**.
 
• The first player or pair to take a **two-point lead **will thereafter** win the game.**
 
• A game used to be played **until score 21, **but that rule was changed by the **ITTF in 2001.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Table tennis, commonly referred to as **ping-pong and whiff-whaff**, is a game in which** two or four players** use little sturdy rackets to strike a lightweight ball across a table back and forth. 
 
• The **International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF), **a global organization established in **1926,** is in charge of overseeing it.​

questions.question: Which of the following devices is used for measuring distance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odometer.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• A device for **calculating the distance **a car has travelled is an odometer.
 
• The odometer is located on the **dashboard **of the car.
 
• An odometer might be **mechanical or digital.**
 
• The majority of mechanical odometers have many** cogs**. A **numerical digit **is represented by each cog.
 
• Through a driving mechanism and cable, the **cogs rotate** in accordance with the **rotation of the wheels.**
 
• In contrast to mechanical odometers, digital odometers employ a** computer chip to track mileage.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gnomon:**

 
 
• It is a gadget designed initially as a time tracking device.
 
• It appears to have been a rod set vertically on a planar surface in its most basic form, then later on a hemisphere's surface.
 
 
 
• **Manometer:**
 
 
• A manometer measures the pressure (static pressure) exerted by a motionless liquid or gas.
 
• It operates on the hydrostatic equilibrium concept.
 
 
 
• **Pyrometer:**
 
 
• ​A pyrometer is a device that detects temperature without having to be in close proximity to the item, i.e. by detecting radiation from the object.

questions.question: Which of the following villages is related to the ‘Bhoodan Movement’ initiated by Vinoba Bhave?
questions.solution:

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vinoba Bhave**, a follower of** Mahatma Gandhi,** founded the** Bhoodan Movement **in **Pochampally village in April 1951.**
 
• The Movement made an effort to persuade **wealthy landowners **to voluntarily **donate a portion of their property** to others who were **without land.**
 
• Bhave was philosophically influenced by **Gram Swarajya and the Sarvodaya movement** of Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• About** 1.9 million hectares** were collected in **just six years.**
 
• Over the **next two decades **the movement took shape of a law called the **Bhoodan Act** and put the **government in charge** of distributing land from the land bank.
 
• Later, the movement evolved into the **Gramdan (village in gift) movement**, when the entirety or a significant portion of a **village's land was donated** by at least **75%** of the locals for equal distribution among all villagers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hogenakkal:**

 
 
• In the Indian state of **Tamil Nadu,** Hogenakkal is a village located in the** Pennagaram taluk of the Dharmapuri district.**
 
• It is a popular tourist destination, famed for its** bathing areas, rented boat trips**, and the moniker** "Niagara Falls of India."**
 
 
 
• **Amrapali:**
 
 
• Amrapali was a renowned **nagarvadhu (royal courtesan**) who lived in the ancient Indian republic of** Vaishali,** which is now Bihar, circa 500 BC.
 
• She attained** arahant status **by practicing the **teachings of the Buddha.**
 
 
 
• **Kumbhari:**
 
 
• The village of Kumbhari is situated in **Maharashtra, India's Solapur district,** in the Solapur South tehsil.

questions.question: _______ wrote the first Sanskrit grammar book named ‘Ashtadhyayi’.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Panini.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **earliest source on Sanskrit grammar **still in existence is the** Ashtadhyayi. **
 
• **It is **a **prehistoric Indian text** that was written sometime between the** fifth and fourth centuries BCE.**
 
• The** Indian grammarian Panini** was the author.
 
• It condenses the **phonetic and grammatical knowledge** that has developed inside the **Vedic religion** into **4,000 sutras.**
 
• **Ashtadhyayi's grammar** has been compared to the **Turing machine,** a** mathematically idealized model** that distils any computing device's logical architecture to its most basic components.
 
• In ancient India, Panini was a** renowned scholar, grammarian, and Sanskrit philologist.**
 
• Panini has been referred to as the** "first descriptive linguist"** and **"the father of linguistics."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Valmiki:**

 
 
• The harbinger-poet Valmiki is renowned in** Sanskrit literature**.
 
• Based on the attribution in the book itself, he is credited with writing the** epic Ramayana, **which has variably been dated to the 5th century BCE and the 1st century BCE.
 
 
 
• **Tulsidas:**
 
 
• Tulsidas, also referred to as **Goswami Tulsidas, **was a** poet** and **Ramanandi Vaishnava Hindu saint.**
 
• The **Hanuman Chalisa **and the** epic Ramcharitmanas**, which is a translation of the Sanskrit Ramayana based on the biography of Rama in the** Awadhi dialect**, are works that bear his name.
 
 
 
• **Kabir:**
 
 
• Hinduism's Bhakti movement was influenced by the writings of **Kabir Das,** an** Indian mystic poet **and** saint** who lived in the 15th century.
 
• His poetry can be found in the** Guru Granth Sahib, the Satguru Granth Sahib of Saint Garib Das, and Kabir Sagar.**

questions.question: Which of the following is a Zaid crop?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muskmelon.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Zaid crops are **small time period crops** that are also referred to as **summer crops **and as **"Grishmkal crops**" in various** Asian regions.**
 
• These are planted from** March to June, **in the period between the Kharif and Rabi seasons.
 
• They need l**onger days for blossoming** and** warm, dry weather** for their **critical growth stage**.
 
• This is** important for farmers** because it provides them with **quick cash** and** fills the gap** between their two main crops, Kharif and Rabi.
 
• **Examples** include cucumbers, pumpkins, bitter gourd, watermelons, muskmelons, sugarcane, groundnuts, and pulses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rabi Crops:**

 
 
• Rabi crops are those that are** cultivated** during the** winter months (October to December) **and **harvested **during the **spring months (April to May).**
 
• These crops require a** warm climate for germination and maturation** of seeds and need a** cold environment for their growth.**
 
• **Winter rain damages the Rabi crop** but benefits the Kharif crop.
 
• Wheat, gram, barley, peas, oats, chickpeas, linseed, mustard, etc. are a few **examples.**
 
 
 
• **​Kharif Crops:**
 
 
• The monsoon season is when crops called **Kharif, monsoon crops, or autumn crops** are grown and harvested.
 
• At the start of the** monsoon season**, the farmer **plants seeds, **and at the end of the season, he **harvests them** i.e., between **September and October.**
 
• For** effective growth,** Kharif crops require a** lot of water and a warm climate.**
 
• **Examples** include cotton, rice, maize, millet, soybeans, and arhar.​

questions.question: In which year did Debendranath Tagore establish the Tattvabodhini Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1839.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• On **October 6, 1839,** the **Tattwabodhini Sabha** was established in **Calcutta** as a breakaway faction of the **Brahmo Samaj**, an organization dedicated to reforming** both Hinduism and Indian society.**
 
• **Debendranath Tagore,** a former member of the Brahmo Samaj and the** eldest child** of prominent **businessman Dwarkanath Tagore,** served as the **organization's founding member.**
 
• **He **later became the** father** of acclaimed polymath** Rabindranath Tagore.**
 
• Debendranath Tagore** disbanded** the Tattwabodhini Sabha and reorganized it as the** Brahmo Samaj in 1859.**
 
• The **Sabha's main goal** was to advance a **more logical and humanist version** of Hinduism based on the **Upanishads,** which make up the** final segment of the Vedas.**

questions.question: The ______ is the primary layer of the rainforest and forms a roof over the two remaining layers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**canopy layer.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **overlapping branches and leaves **of rainforest trees make up the canopy layer**.**
 
• This layer can reach heights of over **100 feet (30 meters) **above the ground.
 
• The rainforest is the richest home for plant and animal life, with scientists estimating that between** 60 and 90 per cent **of it may be found in the **treetops**.
 
• The canopy is home to a wide variety of well-known species, such as **sloths, tiny cats, frogs, lizards, birds, snakes, and monkeys.**
 
• During the** day**, the** canopy is drier and hotter** than other parts of the forest, and the plants and animals that live there are specially adapted for life in the trees.

 
• Canopy layer plants** absorb the light** that penetrates through from the top layer, which is known as the **emergent layer.**
 
• The canopy layer absorbs an estimated** 75-98% of light,** blocking this light from reaching the layers below.
 
• Most of the** rainfall **is captured by the **canopy layer** and very little gets to the plants at the **lower levels. ​**
 
• [IMAGE: https://animalcorner.org/wp-content/img/strata.jpg] ** **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Understory layer:**

 
 
• The understory, a stratum made up of** young trees, short species of trees, shrubs, and soft-stemmed plants**, can be found many** meters below** the bottom of the canopy.
 
• From rainforest to rainforest, the understory** differs greatly**.
 
 
 
• **Forest floor:**
 
 
• The forest floor, also known as **detritus, duff, and the O horizon**, is one of the forest ecosystem's most recognizable characteristics.
 
• It mostly comprises **vegetative elements** that have been** shed, such as leaves, branches, bark, and stems,** which are present above the soil surface in varying states of decomposition.
 
 
 
• **Emergent layer: **
 
 
• The emergent layer is the** uppermost layer **of a rainforest.
 
• This layer experiences** intense sunlight, copious amounts of rain, and strong winds**.
 
• The **tallest trees tower 230 fee**t **(70 m) **above all other plants.

questions.question: The panel of chairpersons in Lok Sabha consists of how many members?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• There can only be** ten chairpersons** in the** Lok Sabha** in India.
 
• They are primarily used to **fill in for speakers **when they are not there.
 
• However, they are** unable to lead** if the **Speaker and Deputy Speaker offices** are vacant.
 
• The** current members **are Arjun Charan Sethi (BJD), M Thambidurai (AIADMK), K V Thomas (Cong), Anandrao Adsul (SS), Hukm Deo Narayan Yadav, Prahlad Joshi, Hukum Singh and Ramen Deka (all BJP), Ratna De (Nag) (Trinamool) and Konakalla Narayan Rao (TDP).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **lower house of India's bicameral Parliament **is known as the **Lok Sabha**, and the **upper house** is known as the **Rajya Sabha.**
 
• There are **545 total seats** in the** Lok Sabha.**
 
• The **Election Commission** will hold elections to fill **543 of these seats.**
 
• If the President decides that the** Anglo-Indian community** has not been adequately represented, persons from that community are nominated to **fill the remaining two seats.**
